tool_input.body:
## Read this part first

**`internal/session` and `internal/mission` gain a real Windows file-locking implementation (`LockFileEx`), not a stub.** That is the substantial change here and the part worth scrutinising — the rest is four small fixes.

`LockFileEx` semantics differ from `flock` in ways that matter: mandatory rather than advisory, handle-scoped rather than fd-scoped, and no atomic shared→exclusive upgrade. `internal/mission`'s shared-vs-exclusive distinction (`AcquireMissionLock` vs `AcquireMissionLockExclusive`) is carried through a `lockShared`/`lockExclusive` mode parameter rather than flattened into one lock — flattening would compile, pass tests, and silently serialise readers.

This repo already had a weaker precedent: `internal/identity` and `internal/claudemd` stub-and-error their flock on Windows. That was deliberately **not** matched. `internal/session`'s lock is what DES-074's session-pointer writes depend on, and a lock that silently doesn't lock is worse than one that doesn't compile. The two older packages should be raised to this standard — filed separately, untouched here.

`GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 go build ./...` now exits 0 for the whole module. darwin and linux builds unaffected; coverage on `internal/session` and `internal/mission` identical before and after.

## The four cluster-1 bugs

**`ethos-lldo`** — `plugin/hooks/commit-msg.sh`'s header claimed "Passthrough when neither env var is set", while the body did a full session lookup on exactly that branch. That lookup is where cross-repo misattribution entered, so the header steered readers away from the live defect. Rewritten to match the code, including DES-074's silent/loud split.

**`ethos-4pvt`** — `session end` now hints `unset ETHOS_SESSION`. The asymmetry was that `session start` prints the export, so the command that sets it told you and the command that invalidates it didn't. The bead's filed symptom was stale — DES-074 already made a leftover export fail loud rather than degrade silently — so a regression pins that too.

**`ethos-gu3p`** — `session start --persona <unknown>` exited 0 and wrote a roster keyed on a handle resolving to nothing; the typo then never surfaced. Now validated before anything is minted. Deliberately scoped to `session start`, **not** `iam`, where existing tests key participants on free-form labels by design.

**`ethos-cm2r` / `ethos-qtp2` / `ethos-298s`** — the Windows work above. cm2r's acceptance was always "blocking full GOOS=windows builds", so it closes all three.

## Review findings, fixed in-branch

Three findings on the first push, two of them defects in the fixes themselves:

- **The end hint fired on any set variable**, not only when it named the session actually ended. `session end --session A` with `ETHOS_SESSION=B` deleted A and told the operator to clear live session B — destroying their context, and outside Claude Code their only discovery channel. Found independently by two reviewers. We fixed advice that didn't help and shipped advice that harmed.
- **The persona check was `Exists()`** — an `os.Stat`. Malformed YAML, a load error, or a `kind` outside {human, agent} all passed to the roster write. Now `Load()` + `Validate()`, with tests for both cases.
- **The Windows walk swallowed real API errors** as "pid not found". Now only `ERROR_NO_MORE_FILES` means walked-to-the-end; everything else propagates.

## Verification

Detached CI simulation — clean `git archive`, `setsid`, all `CLAUDE_*` stripped — run by both the implementer and the leader independently: **27 ok / 0 FAIL / 1 no-test-files**.

`make check` green after every commit. Every new test verified failing against pre-fix code first.

## Known, out of scope

`GOOS=windows go vet ./...` still fails on pre-existing test build-tag mismatches (e.g. `tombstone_purge_test.go` is untagged but calls `testStore()` from `!windows`-tagged `store_test.go`). Previously unreachable because the package didn't compile on Windows at all; surfaced by this change. `make check` never runs vet under `GOOS=windows`. Filed rather than fixed.

tool_input.message:
Pushed dcf970a and rewrote the PR description to put the Windows locking at the top rather than buried — which immediately earned the scrutiny I wanted. Two new Bugbot findings, both in the new Windows code, both real. Fix on the same branch, don't push.

**D — Access-denied PIDs treated as dead.** `internal/session/store_windows.go`, `isProcessAlive`.

Bugbot: it returns false whenever `os.FindProcess` fails, and on Windows `OpenProcess` fails with access-denied for a process owned by another user. So a live process owned by someone else reads as dead.

This is the dangerous one and it is worth being precise about why. `isProcessAlive` gates `PurgeCurrent`'s removal of session pointer files — the guard that stops a concurrent session's SessionStart from purging a LIVE session's pointer. If a live process reads as dead, that guard opens and the pointer gets purged out from under a running session. That is ethos-vqwn's failure class arriving through a new door on a new platform: a session losing its identity because something concluded, wrongly, that it was gone.

Distinguish access-denied (`ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED`) from genuinely-not-found (`ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER` is what OpenProcess gives for a dead PID). Access-denied means the process EXISTS and you cannot open it — treat as alive. Only not-found means dead. Fail closed: when you cannot tell, treat as alive, because the cost of a false "dead" is a purged live session and the cost of a false "alive" is a stale pointer that self-heals at the next SessionStart. Asymmetric, so pick the safe side.

**E — LockFileEx fails on append-only handles.** `internal/mission/trace.go`, `appendTraceSummary`.

It opens `missions.jsonl` with `O_APPEND|O_WRONLY` and then takes the lock. `LockFileEx` requires a handle with appropriate access rights and does not reliably accept an append-only handle. Verify the actual behaviour rather than reasoning about it — write a small probe if that is fastest — then either open with the access `LockFileEx` needs, or take the lock on a separate handle/lockfile. Say which you chose and why.

This is the class of thing that only shows up at runtime on Windows, which nobody here runs, so a compile-clean build proves nothing about it. Given that, a test that actually exercises the locking path on Windows would be worth more than another build check — if that is not feasible in this repo's CI, say so plainly and I will note the limitation in the PR rather than let a green build imply coverage it does not have.

Same process: failing test first where feasible, `make check` per commit, detached gate with both counts, and re-run `GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 go build ./...` (full, not just internal/process — you own the whole build now).

I am replying to and resolving the finding-C thread myself since that fix already landed.
